landing.h1: You send. You wait. Offerly remembers for you.
landing.lead: A job-application tracker. You forward it the mail from job boards, and it records who replied and what you are still waiting on. No spreadsheet, and no password to your mailbox.
landing.micro: No mailbox passwords. No portal scraping. Nothing sent in your name.
landing.peek.w3: Something has to be done by hand
landing.problem.h2: Job hunting falls apart in the details, not the big decisions
landing.problem.1: You send twelve applications and lose track of which CV went where.
landing.problem.2: One employer asks for gross monthly, the next for net hourly, the third for a B2B rate.
landing.problem.3: An offer expires while it sits on your “maybe” list.
landing.problem.4: A reply arrives, gets buried under job alerts, and you answer four days late.
landing.problem.5: You never learn which CV version actually gets responses.
landing.problem.close: A spreadsheet records these things. It does not notice them.
landing.how.h2: From advert to answer, in five steps
landing.how.lead: The register, the history and the dashboard are already built. These five steps are what keep them filled.
landing.how.d1: Forwarded from a job-board alert, or typed in by hand.
landing.how.t2: It lands in an inbox to sort
landing.how.d2: Keep it or drop it — one click, and never in your private mailbox.
landing.how.d3: A CV picked for the offer, and the form's questions filled in with what you already wrote down once.
landing.how.t4: You read it, change it, send it
landing.how.d4: Nothing goes out without you. Offerly prepares; you send.
landing.how.d5: An acknowledgement, a refusal, an invitation — the register updates itself.
landing.features.h2: Six things Offerly does for you
landing.features.lead: Four work from day one and are free. Two — the ones marked Plus — happen without you.
landing.features.d1: Every application is one row: company, role, which CV went out, what you quoted, how long the offer stays open. Come back in six months and you can still see what happened to it.
landing.features.d2: Instead of the whole list you get a few things for today: offers about to close, applications that have gone silent, and forms left half-finished.
landing.features.d3: Notice period, salary expectations, the GDPR clause — write them once, then copy. You never have to remember what you told the last company.
landing.features.d4: You get a separate address and forward job-board alerts to it. They land here instead of your mailbox — already split into role, company, city and salary.
landing.features.d5: Mail from an employer finds the application it belongs to. When that is obvious, the status changes on its own. When it is not, we ask you.
landing.features.d6: What share of applications get a reply — separately for each CV version, each board and each salary bracket. That is how you learn which CV to keep sending.
landing.stats.h2: Which CV version actually draws answers
landing.stats.lead: You could count this by hand. Nobody does.
landing.stats.quote: “The ‘Sales B2B’ version draws a reply nearly four times as often as the general one.”
landing.privacy.h2: Your job search is nobody else's business
landing.privacy.d1: No Gmail OAuth, no IMAP passwords. You get a private address, and a filter in your own mail decides what reaches it. Offerly never sees the rest.
landing.privacy.t2: Nobody else can see your data
landing.privacy.d2: Every table in the database has Row Level Security switched on. Even if the code had a bug, the database would simply refuse to hand over another person's rows.
landing.privacy.d3: No fonts, icons, analytics or CDN. A stylesheet from someone else's server would tell them you are job hunting.
landing.privacy.d4: Every application and answer as plain CSV, whenever you like. Closing the account deletes everything at once — no hidden copy, no row quietly marked as deleted.
landing.pricing.h2: Offerly charges for what it does, never for what you put in
landing.pricing.free_lead: Everything needed to run a job search by hand, without a limit and without a card.
landing.pricing.f1: Unlimited applications, offers, companies and notes
landing.pricing.f2: The whole of “today” — deadlines, silence, unfinished forms
landing.pricing.f3: Form answers with copy-to-clipboard, two CV versions
landing.pricing.f4: Response rate and where applications go
landing.pricing.f5: CSV export, account deletion, password recovery — never behind a payment
landing.pricing.plus_lead: Everything that happens without you — and the numbers you cannot count by hand.
landing.pricing.p3: Reminders by email and a Monday summary
landing.pricing.p4: Statistics per CV version, board and salary bracket
landing.pricing.note: There is no checkout and none is planned — plans are granted by hand, the same way invites are. When a plan ends the data stays: readable, editable, exportable. Only the automation stops.
landing.not.h2: Four things Offerly does not do
landing.not.1d: Job boards forbid it and ban accounts for it — and it would be your account.
landing.not.2d: Applications go out under your name, so you press send.
landing.not.3: No mail sent in your name.
landing.not.3d: Follow-ups to an employer are drafted, never sent.
landing.not.4d: You forward only what you choose to forward.
landing.faq.h2: The questions that keep coming back
landing.faq.a1: No. There is no OAuth and no IMAP password. You get a private address and set a filter in your own mail that forwards job alerts and employer replies to it — nothing else ever reaches us.
landing.faq.q2: What happens when my plan ends?
landing.faq.a2: The data stays — all of it, readable, editable and exportable, forever. Only the automation stops: no new offers collected, no replies matched, no reminders sent.
landing.faq.q3: Will it apply to jobs for me?
landing.faq.a3: It prepares — the CV, the answers, the message — and then stops. You read what was prepared, change anything you disagree with, and send it yourself.
landing.faq.q4: How do I get an invite code?
landing.faq.a4: Write to kontakt@offerly.com.pl. Offerly is in early development, so accounts are opened from codes — they go out in small batches, and you get a note when yours is ready.
landing.faq.a5: Both, everywhere — the interface language is a setting on your account, and it changes the whole app, not just this page.
landing.road.h2: Where this is going, in order
landing.road.1: Auth, application registry, statuses, CV versions, dashboard.
landing.road.2: Email forwarding, alert parsers, reply matching, reminders.
landing.road.3: CV generation from a structured profile, tailoring per offer, public API.
landing.road.4: Assisted applying, a mobile client, self-hosted deployment.
landing.end.h2: Codes go out in small batches. We write when yours is ready.
landing.end.lead: No newsletter and no campaign — one message with a code, and nothing else.
landing.end.note: This writes to kontakt@offerly.com.pl. A form that stores addresses comes later — we would rather not collect them before there is somewhere safe to keep them.
landing.footer.tagline: Job application tracker · in Polish and English · MIT licence
landing.privacy.d5: The text of forwarded board alerts goes to Google Gemini to pull out the role, company, city and salary. Only alerts go — never an employer's reply, your notes, or a CV. Every field comes back checked against the message, and anything not literally in it is thrown away.
